stories.title: Brazil's Lula wins historic fourth term presidency
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term, the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. However, his opponent Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, refused to accept defeat and said he would ask for the result to be annulled due to a ruling from a Supreme Court justice that extended voting for two hours. Mr Bolsonaro led the election's first round but lost in the runoff by over four million votes, rattling Brazilian financial markets which had bet on his victory. His refusal to concede defeat has echoes of his father's reaction after losing to Mr Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never accepted his loss and was later sentenced by the Supreme Court to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup to remain in power. The scale of Flavio Bolsonaro's loss to Mr Lula - by more than twice his father's losing margin - and the fact his campaign also asked for an extension due to rains in the conservative-leaning south make any annulment unlikely, analysts said.

stories.title: Where to next after Triple Lock passes first Dáil vote?
stories.summary: The 'Triple Lock' has become one of the most contentious topics in this Government's Programme for Government, in Dáil Éireann, within the Fianna Fáil party and on the streets. But it all began when legislation was passed in 1960 to allow Irish troops to be sent abroad, after joining the United Nations five years previously. These missions would only be backed by the United Nations and for decades that meant Irish participation in peacekeeping has depended on UN backing. This rule was restated as the 'Triple Lock' at the start of the century after concerns that the Nice and Lisbon Treaties would undermine neutrality, with Government parties back then stressing its importance. Under the rule, no more than 12 troops can be deployed on an active mission overseas without a decision by the Government, the approval of the Dáil and the authorisation of the United Nations. However, because the Government usually has a majority in the Dáil, the first two conditions are largely one and the same, and UN approval became key.

stories.title: Minister says meeting with solicitors likely next week
stories.summary: The Minister for Justice has confirmed that he has "engaged" with solicitors and that a meeting is likely next week. Speaking at the launch of One In Four's annual report, Jim O’Callaghan said letters had been exchanged. A majority of solicitors working in criminal legal aid across the country have been in dispute with Mr O'Callaghan since a new €520 flat-fee payment for legal aid cases was introduced in July. Mr O’Callaghan insists that legal aid continues to be granted by the courts; solicitors continue to provide representation, and defendants continue to receive legal services throughout the State. This week, the minister said he would meet the Law Society of Ireland regarding the dispute. In a letter to President of the Law Society of Ireland Rosemarie Loftus, Mr O'Callaghan said he had instructed his officials to "organise a meeting in the coming days to hear your viewpoint and specific concerns".

stories.title: Euro zone growth slows to 4-month low amid French turmoil
stories.summary: Growth across the euro zone's private sector slowed to its weakest pace in four months in October, driven by an energy-driven rise in costs and a renewed contraction in France amid political and financial pressures, a survey showed today. The S&P global flash euro zone Composite PMI ⁠Output Index fell to 51.9 in October from September's 53.1, its lowest reading since June and lower than all forecasts in a Reuters poll which had predicted a modest dip to 52.7. "Key to the broader slowdown is the further escalation of inflationary pressures seen during the month," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Input costs are rising sharply again, the rate of increase surging in manufacturing on the back of higher energy prices, causing firms to push selling prices higher in order to protect margins," he said. Input costs accelerated for the second consecutive month linked to higher energy, fuel and transport costs in part due to the Middle ‌East war. Despite this, firms raised their ⁠selling prices at a slower pace than in September, suggesting some margin compression. "Higher interest rates are also starting to take a toll, dampening demand, and the picture of sustained growth and stubbornly elevated inflation from the October flash PMI will likely add to further speculation of more aggressive policy tightening from the ECB," Williamson added.

stories.title: Clashes in France as hundreds of thousands protest
stories.summary: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets of France as a vastly reinforced security presence appeared to have averted a repeat of last weekend's unrest, despite isolated clashes in several cities. Some 110,000 people marched peacefully through the French capital, according to police numbers. Waving flags, they denounced the growing cost of living and rising inequality. "Down with the state, the police and the fascists," the crowd chanted. At the end of the march, police fired tear gas and used water cannon to try to disperse small groups of hooded youths, but the violence was far less than last Saturday, when looters and vandals went on the rampage in Paris. Clashes also flared in Lyon, Bordeaux and Grenoble, while police fired volleys of tear gas at demonstrators in Clermont-Ferrand, Lille and Nice. In France's second city, Marseille, youths dragged large metal sheets to block a street, set fire to rubbish bins, and hurled rocks and bottles at riot police, with the confrontations continuing as night fell.

stories.title: Brosnan: 'Patience' key to Dr Crokes 15th Kerry title
stories.summary: "Patience" was the key ingredient to Dr Crokes securing their 15th Kerry SFC title against Kenmare Shamrocks, according to Brian Looney and captain Tony Brosnan. Kenmare Shamrocks were appearing in their first ever county final and their opponents' experience showed as a late burst of scores saw them win 2-14 to 1-24. Kenmare led for large swathes of the game, including going up by seven points in the first seven minutes, but nine unanswered points late into the second half swung the game in favour of Dr. Crokes. "David Shaw was immense there today. We have kickers all around the pitch and we've probably learned from the club final here six weeks ago where our shooting wasn't to the standards that we usually have them and basically we paid the penalty and we lost that game. "So we knew we just needed to be patient. We've been patient in all the games and it served us well. So we knew when it got down to the nitty gritty of the game we had the kickers and the patience to get over the line." Looney, who now has nine club titles to his name, echoed his captain's comments: "It's just showing a bit of patience. Kenmare are a really good side but I think it gets to a point in a game where no matter who you're playing it opens up a little bit and you can create those pockets of space and I think there's been occasions where we've been guilty of forcing it or taking the wrong shot options.

stories.title: London SHC: Last-gasp heroics see Brothers Pearse win
stories.summary: Last-gasp heroics from Malcolm Flannery saw Brothers Pearse dig deep and come from behind in injury time to win their 13th London Senior Hurling Championship title and break Sean Treacy’s hearts at McGovern Park in Ruislip. The opening 10 minutes of the decider were fiercely contested. Sean Treacy’s, chasing their first title since 2002, landed the first blow through Adam Jordan before Brothers Pearse’s Paul Kennedy replied in the eighth minute. That would be the north-west Londoners’ last score for more than 10 minutes as their opponents from south of the river began to find their rhythm in a stop-start game. Jack Fagan restored Treacy’s lead with a monster effort, followed by two points from Danny Buckley. Jordan and Michael Roche then stretched the south Londoners’ advantage to five. Kennedy registered his side’s second point in the 20th minute to interrupt Treacy’s scoring run. Another Roche point followed before Eoin O’Neill’s side sparked into life. Kennedy, Aidan O’Brien and Flannery added points before some lovely interplay between Kennedy and O’Brien created an opening for Mark Kilgannon, who superbly flicked the ball into the net to leave just a point between the sides as the interval approached.

stories.title: Shels secure Europa Cup spot despite late Galway rally
stories.summary: All-Island and FAI Cup winners Shelbourne secured second place and a spot in the UEFA Women's Europa Cup for next season as they shared the spoils with Galway United in a bruising battle to bring the curtain down on another Women’s Premier Division season. First half goals from Alex Kavanagh and Isabella Flocchini had Shels in cruise control but two injury-time goals from Emma Doherty and Lucy Jane Grant saw Galway rescue a point in dramatic fashion but proved too little too late as Shels better goal difference saw them over the line. It all came down to this, a straight shootout for the much coveted second place. If a week-long wait of nerves and anticipation wasn’t bad enough, an extra day delay due to the stormy conditions only whetted appetites further. With what turned out to be a crucial the ace up their sleeve of a better goal difference, a draw would have been enough for the visitors prior to kick off but with their hostile hosts itching at revenge for the All-Island Cup defeat at Tolka Park, the double winners knew they couldn’t rest on their laurels. At a blustery Eamonn Deacy Park, it was Phil Trill’s who looked to draw first blood causing an almighty goalmouth scramble that saw both Isabella Beletic and Abbie Callanan have shots blocked as the Reds - wearing white - bodies were thrown on the line. The visitors began to get a foothold and enjoyed large spells of possession but were met by the physical box-midfield of the home side as Amanda McQuillan remained untested early on.

stories.title: McMillan: 'Powers that be' to look at foul play incident
stories.summary: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan said "the powers that be" will decide on the outcome of an allegation of serious foul play, after his side's 24-18 defeat to Leinster at Aviva Stadium. Munster's injury-hit squad felt the full force of Leinster's internationals in the second half of their interpro, as McMillan's side saw their 13-0 lead wiped out by four Leinster tries. There was a major flashpoint late in the first half, when Munster's Gavin Coombes alleged he had been grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck. Referee Andrew Brace stopped play during the 39th minute and spent some time speaking to his TMO, who searched for footage of the alleged incident to no avail. While the officials weren't able to identify the incident during the game, it may still be referred to the citing commissioner. "It's one of those things that we leave in the hands of the powers that be," Munster head coach McMillan said.

stories.title: Wexford Festival Opera - watch The Gambler by Sergei Prokofiev
stories.summary: We proudly present a live presentation from this year's Wexford Festival Opera - The Gambler by Sergei Prokofiev, with a libretto by the composer after Fyodor Dostoevsky. With its jagged, modernist score, The Gambler offers a chillingly relevant look at the price of desire. Place your bets on a night of operatic intensity and join us for this rare, visceral revival. Written in 1917 during the First World War when the composer was 26 years old and still considered to be in his enfant terrible phase, the opera was not performed until 1929. Based on Fyodor Dostoevsky’s 1866 novella, in this new production – marking the Wexford debuts of director Ivan Popovski and conductor Valentin Uryupin – nervous obsession spirals into self-destruction. Set in 1865 in the fictional German spa town of Roulettenburg, everything is deliberately artificial. The opera follows the protagonist, Alexei, a young tutor, as he spirals into gambling debt while being obsessed with his employer’s stepdaughter, Polina. In the final act, the casino itself emerges as the central character, controlling the destiny of those consumed by their passion for the roulette wheel, like moths to a flame. Prokofiev intended the work as a reaction against Romantic lyricism, instead preferring to create ‘an opera in the declamatory style’, closer in technique to the stageworks of Dargomyzhsky and Mussorgsky which set musical prose in natural speech rhythms. stories.title: Oscar favourite Wildwood works on many levels, say stars
stories.summary: Peyton Elizabeth Lee and Jacob Tremblay have seen the just-released fantasy hailed as a landmark in animated filmmaking as studio LAIKA (Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls) and director Travis Knight champion stop-motion animation with their finest two hours to date. Wildwood tells the story of bolshy teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee - Andi Mack, Doogie Kameāloha, M.D.) and her bumbling pal Curtis (Jacob Tremblay - Room, Wonder) as they desperately search for Prue's baby brother - taken by a murder of crows and brought deep into the no-go lands that surround their Portland home. It mixes action and humour with themes of loss and belonging as Prue realises everyone needs some help from time to time while Curtis discovers he is stronger than he thinks. "I think there's a lot of mature themes to the film. So, this is the first film [from LAIKA] with a PG-13 rating, so that means a lot. But I think this definitely is a film a lot of people can enjoy." "The story works on many different levels that I think different people of different ages can relate to," continued co-star Lee. "The animation medium is so special because I think it allows you to connect with young people and tell stories that have darker thematic elements while it still feeling exciting and magical and fun.

stories.title: Embracing the history, flavours, and spectacular views of Türkiye
stories.summary: Tara Povey experiences the crystal-clear waters, ancient ruins and delicious flavours of Türkiye. Turkey officially became Türkiye in 2022, and I didn't even notice. Despite Istanbul sitting on my travel bucket list for years, I’d never visited. I knew the trope of people going to Türkiye with receding hairlines or dodgy teeth and coming back looking like reality TV stars, but that’s as far as my knowledge went. Then, one day, after some dramatic romantic ups and downs that you may have read about, I met a kind, handsome Turkish man and suddenly I was learning about the Ottoman Empire, and how Türkiye sent aid to Ireland during the Famine. At the end of September we visited Türkiye together for the first time. We both knew my melanin-deprived skin would be no match for the Turkish heat during peak summer when temperatures reach up to 40°C. We flew direct from Dublin to Antalya with Sun Express, picked up our rental car and set off to explore the turquoise coast. Konyaalti is a stunning 7km stretch of pebbly beach with crystal-clear water and the Taurus mountains acting as a dramatic backdrop. We stayed in an apartment in Konyaalti just a few minutes' walk from the beach.

stories.title: Irish troops should be in new Lebanon mission - McEntee
stories.summary: Irish troops should be deployed to Lebanon as part of a new EU mission and be involved in both peacekeeping and peace enforcement duties, according to the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Defence Helen McEntee. Troops are currently deployed as part of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) but the mission ends at the end of this year following a Security Council vote, and the Defence Forces are due to withdraw by Easter. A new EU mission to replace UNIFIL was passed by EU Foreign Ministers last month, however, Minister McEntee said: "We will not be able to do that if the Triple Lock is not reformed." Asked if Irish troops participating in a peacekeeping role or peace enforcement role, Minister McEntee replied: "It's likely to be both. And it's important to stress that it currently the case now. "There's a misconception, or an attempt to suggest, that our troops are on the ground in one context, and one context only. Our troops are involved in peace enforcement at the moment." Asked if she would use the guillotine to ensure the Triple Lock legislation passes the Oireachtas before Christmas, which would no longer require a UN mandate before Irish troops could be deployed, the minister replied that she did not intend to rush matters but added: "I do plan to and would like to have this done by the end of the year."

stories.title: Halloween to generate over €40m across Ireland
stories.summary: Fáilte Ireland estimates that Halloween events will generate more than €40m for local communities and tourism businesses across the island of Ireland. Over 320,000 domestic and international visitors attended over 800 events last year and it is hoped that figure will increase this year. "Halloween did not begin in Hollywood," said Azeta Seery, Festivals and Events Manager at Fáilte Ireland. "It has its roots in the ancient tradition of Samhain, which spans over almost 2,000 years ago here in Ireland." Over the last number of years tourism chiefs here have developed a new tourism season around Halloween in a bid to increase visitor numbers. In 2025, it said that events attracted over 322,000 domestic and international visitors.

stories.title: No measure can ease pain of scoliosis failures - minister
stories.summary: The Minister for Health has acknowledged that no measures the Government may introduce will alleviate the pain endured by those affected by failures in spina bifida and scoliosis services. She told the Dáil that stakeholders will be consulted by her officials, who will work with the Attorney General to draft terms of reference for a commission of inquiry. The minister was speaking during Statements on Children's Health Ireland (CHI), which was also attended in the visitors' gallery by some of those who have been advocating for action on the matter. Ms Carroll MacNeill said that she received the final scoping report on 9 September, and expressed her gratitude to Remy Farrell SC for his efforts to "capture the pain" and "very real frustration" of those affected. She noted that a commission of investigation, as recommended by Mr Farrell, allows for greater flexibility than a tribunal, including private hearings. She noted that witnesses can request whether to have their testimony heard in public or private.

stories.title: Lidl to invest €420m across Munster, creating 500 jobs
stories.summary: Lidl has today announced a €420m investment across Munster, which the supermarket group said will create more than 500 permanent jobs. €306m of the investment is earmarked for Co Cork, the company added. At the centre of the programme is Lidl's new €200m regional distribution centre at Little Island in Cork, alongside plans for 14 new stores across Munster and the redevelopment of 10 existing locations. As well as creating 500 jobs, including 250 in Cork, the company said the investment will also support more than 4,500 construction jobs across the 25 developments. Lidl currently employs more than 1,300 people across Munster and once the new investment is delivered, its permanent workforce in the region is expected to exceed 1,800. The €420m regional programme represents a significant part of Lidl's wider €600m five-year investment programme in Ireland, through which the retailer intends to open up to 35 additional stores around the country.

stories.title: Brazil extends voting hours after public transport issues
stories.summary: Brazil's Supreme Court extended voting in the country's presidential election by two hours, leading the electoral authority to pause a vote count that had already started publishing early-stage results. The election pits leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls were initially set to close at 5pm (8pm Irish time) and will now close at 7pm, after Supreme Justice Cristiano Zanin accepted a request by Mr Lula's campaign to extend voting, pointing to public transportation issues in three cities in the state of Bahia. Mr Justice Zanin's decision landed right around the 5pm cutoff, when the electoral court had already started publishing results that showed Mr Lula leading Mr Bolsonaro with 0.25% of ballot counted. Mr Lula had 57.66% of votes, compared with 42.34% for Mr Bolsonaro, the early count showed. After the ruling, the TSE said it would pause the vote count to allow for the extended voting window to close.

stories.title: Cullen hints at more switches after Sheehan side-quest
stories.summary: Interprovincial derbies are seldom a signpost for trying out new combinations on a whim, but that was the position that Leinster found themselves in last week. With Caelan Doris on the long-term absentee list, and Jack Conan picking up an untimely bang in the Champions Cup win over ASM Clermont Auvergne, Cullen rolled the dice with one of his most dynamic forwards. Some 140 games into his professional career, Ireland hooker Dan Sheehan was deployed at number eight for Saturday night's win over Munster. The test Lion from 2025 played back-row growing up, and took to the task at hand at ease. The 28-year-old made 17 carries, the most of any Leinster player, and nine tackles across his 80 minute outing. It impressed many in attendance, and most importantly, the Leinster coach who was full of praise for his captain. "I thought he was very, very good", Cullen said of Sheehan after the game. "In terms of carrying the fight in the game, which is, you know, getting his hands on the ball in attack and being hungry to make hits defensively as well.

stories.title: Women's club wrap: Kilmacud on track for fifth SFC crown
stories.summary: Kilmacud Crokes remain on course for a fifth straight AIB Leinster SFC crown after they advanced to the semi-finals after they got the better of Carlow opponents Old Leighlin at Páirc de Burca by 2-18 to 0-4. Clodagh Lohan hit the net twice as Longford Slashers got the better of Offaly's Ballinamere Durrow by 2-13 to 3-1, while Wicklow’s Tinahely recorded a 2-9 to 0-10 victory as they saw off the challenge of Westmeath’s Milltown. Kate Flood hit 0-6 and Maggie Holland hit a late two pointer as the Louth champions, Naomh Padraig, defeated Eadestown of Kildare and booked a place in the final four. In the Leinster SFC semi-finals, Kilmacud Crokes will face Naomh Padraig and Tinahely will face Longford Slashers. The 2026 AIB Munster Senior Championship final will be contested by Cork’s Aghada and Waterford’s Gaultier after their respective semi-final wins this weekend. Aghada defeated reigning champions Southern Gaels in a high scoring encounter. Mary Leahy hit the net twice for the Cork champions while Clare Walsh, Abigail Ring and captain Roisin Phelan also converted. Southern Gaels battled hard with Siofra O’Shea, Rachel Dwyer and Aoife Dwyer all converting to the net, but Aghada were not to be denied.

stories.title: Liverpool quartet click to clip soaring Brighton's wings
stories.summary: Liverpool's expensively-assembled front four finally clicked into gear as they beat Brighton 2-0 to record their first home Premier League win of the season. The trio of €100 million-plus signings Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz – and Cody Gakpo – found a connection which fans have been hoping will succeed in breaking down defences against whom they struggled during their disappointing title defence. They do not come more miserly than the Seagulls as Fabian Hurzeler’s side may be the top flight’s leading scorers but they also know how to keep the back door tightly shut and these were the first goals conceded in all competitions in over nine hours. Wirtz was denied the credit for the 17th-minute opener due to the deflection off Pascal Gross but there was no doubting Isak’s sixth goal in seven league appearances four minutes later from a Barcola cross. Strong contributions from the France international and Gakpo on the flanks ensured Brighton were never entirely comfortable in a first half in which they started the brighter. By the 77th minute only Gakpo remained but with the visitors starting to cause problems – and Chelsea arriving on Wednesday in the Carabao Cup – changes were necessary.

stories.title: Leinster comeback wears Munster down at the Aviva
stories.summary: Leinster overpowered Munster in the second half at Aviva Stadium, as Leo Cullen's side came from 13-0 down to record a bonus-point 24-18 win against their rivals. Tries for Tommy O'Brien, Ryan Baird, Charlie Tector and Jamie Osborne gave the defending champions their second URC win of the season, as Munster's hefty injury list proved decisive down the stretch. While both sides' internationals will head off to Ireland camp this week, there could be a significant fallout in the days ahead, with an allegation of foul play late in the first half seeing play stopped for several minutes. Munster's Gavin Coombes alleged he was grabbed in the groin area by a Leinster player at a ruck, and while referee Andrew Brace stopped play for several minutes to consult his TMO, they could not find a conclusive angle to pursue it, although the incident could still be referred to the citing commissioner. Munster had been dominant in the first half, as their backrow tormented Leinster at the breakdown, and they were 13-0 in front after 28 minutes, with Shane Daly racing in for a stunning try, and 20-year-old out-half Charlie O'Shea kicking a conversion and two penalties on another impressive outing. Clayton McMillan's side had used the scrum as a major weapon so far this season, but they were on the backfoot at the setpiece as Andrew Porter got on top of Kieran Brookes, which proved crucial in Leinster's second half comeback.

stories.title: They did not go quietly - inside Ireland's last witch trial
stories.summary: It’s May 2026 and we are driving on a sunny weekday afternoon to the Islandmagee Peninsula, twenty miles north of Belfast. As the waters of Larne Lough, the body of water which separates Islandmagee from the mainland, comes into view the question arises, what do we believe really happened here on this remote spit of land back in 1711? The history books tell us that a young Presbyterian woman named Mary Dunbar was showing all the signs of demonic possession. Over a period of days, she named eight local women as witches, claiming they were responsible for her torment. The people of Islandmagee, at that time mostly Presbyterians of Scottish descent, believed Mary's accusations and the eight women were arrested, put on trial and found guilty. They are on record as fiercely protesting their innocence in court. Today the peninsula is a tourist attraction for visitors to the Gobbins, a cliff walkway suspended over the Irish Sea. Yet, there are traces of its past written into the landscape; stone built cottages clinging to hillsides, churches dating back to the 1500s, and a landmark steeped in folklore: the Witches’ Rocking Stone, a boulder overlooking Brown’s Bay.

stories.title: Harlan Coben has 'imposter syndrome' about his work
stories.summary: Writer Harlan Coben has admitted he feels an "imposter syndrome" around his work, which has spawned series such as Myron Bolitar. The 64-year-old, who has seen novels such as The Stranger, Fool Me Once and Safe adapted for the screen by Netflix, said he thought only bad writers believed in themselves. Speaking to Lauren Laverne on BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs, he said: "I actually think only bad writers think they’re good. "We all have a little bit of that imposter syndrome, and what’s interesting is it sounds like a paradox, but it’s not. "Because on the one hand, I’m always like, 'I suck, I’m terrible, I hate this’, but at the exact same time I have the hubris to think ‘you’re going to spend 20 pounds, and you’re going to spend five or six hours reading it, or listening to it on audio, and you should’. "And those seem to be a complete contradiction, but they’re not inside of a writer."

stories.title: 15 of the best coffee shops in Ireland
stories.summary: Ireland's coffee scene is booming and winning acclaim on a global scale. Here, food and travel content creator Éadaoin Fitzmaurice shares her pick of the top 15 coffee shops around Ireland, so you not only have new places to visit, but delicious drinks waiting for you there. There's nothing quite like arriving in a new town or county during a staycation and tracking down the best coffee around - a place that will become a daily ritual for the duration of your stay. Grá Linn, located in the coastal village of Fethard-on-Sea, has become a gathering place for locals, weekend wanderers and those tracing the quieter corners of Wexford. Here you’ll find a speciality coffee culture with genuine small-town warmth, as well as great seasonal brunch dishes and pastries. Large windows frame the rhythm of village life outside, while inside the focus is on quality ingredients and thoughtful service. Whether you're fuelling up before exploring the Hook Peninsula, or returning from a sea swim at Baginbun Beach, Grá Linn is the perfect stop. Hey Darling has brought a distinctly modern energy to Kildare's coffee scene. With three branches across Sallins, Naas and Kill, this stylish coffee shop blends excellent coffee with a sharp eye for design, creating a space that feels as considered as the drinks being served.

stories.title: Iran to hold security talks with Saudi, Pakistan, Turkey
stories.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan will hold talks on regional security with Iranian officials today in Tehran, Iranian and Saudi authorities said. The meeting follows eight months of war in the Middle East and recent US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks against Iran. "As agreed, Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will participate in this meeting," said Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. In an interview with state television, Mr Kani said the meeting will also include Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Dr Rayed Krimly confirmed that the kingdom's defence minister was heading a delegation to Tehran on Monday. "The visit comes as part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement countries for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis," Krimly said in a post on X.

stories.title: Immigration process for skilled workers to be streamlined
stories.summary: A new policy to streamline the process for highly-skilled workers seeking to live and work in Ireland will be piloted next year. Currently, applicants must engage with multiple Government processes when they want to live and work in Ireland. But the pilot project, expected to start in the first half of next year, aims to make the process simpler. It will test the new Single Permit Procedure for applicants under the Critical Skills Employment Permit (CSEP) scheme. This scheme aims to attract highly-skilled workers to sectors here that are experiencing labour shortages. This includes attracting workers to jobs like nursing, software development and IT.

stories.title: Russian embassy criticises McEntee over Dáil statement
stories.summary: The Minister for Foreign Affairs and Defence has been accused of making "reprehensible and misleading" comments in the Dáil about Russia's role in the UN Security Council and its approach to UN peacekeeping missions. The Russian Embassy in Ireland took issue with Helen McEntee's statement this week that the current "Triple Lock" legislation allows Russia, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, "to have a say over which peacekeeping missions we can send our troops to". In a statement, the embassy said: "Contrary to her assertions, the UN Security Council does not vote on what countries take part in a peacekeeping mission - its composition is agreed in the course of multilateral consultations conducted by the UN Secretariat and the interested UN member-countries." It added: "The allegations by Minister McEntee are reprehensible and misleading, grossly distorting the substance and the meaning of procedures provided by the UN Charter." The Russian Embassy also took issue with her remarks that Russia is "attacking European member-states, including Germany, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Poland". "The Minister's speculations over Russia's 'attacks' on the EU countries are totally baseless, dangerously provocative and unacceptable," the statement said.

stories.title: Mortgage drawdowns by FTB hit highest level since 2008
stories.summary: Mortgage drawdowns by first-time buyers are at the highest level since 2008, according to the mortgage drawdowns figures released by the Banking and Payment Federation Ireland. A total of 14,217 mortgages to the value of almost €4.6 billion were drawn down by borrowers in the months of July, August and September. This is a 13% increase in volume compared to the same period last year. Most of this activity was driven by first-time buyers - with 8,164 mortgages they accounted for 60% of all drawdowns in the third quarter. "Our latest figures show continued momentum across the mortgage market, with growth in drawdowns across every customer segment during the third quarter of 2026," said Brian Hayes, chief executive at BPFI. Remortgaging and switching activities saw a sharp rise as well.

stories.title: Israel demolishes homes in West Bank after fatal attack
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said Israel would lock down Hebron in the West Bank, go house to house and demolish homes after the Israeli military ⁠said Palestinian attackers killed two soldiers at a military checkpoint near the city. The Israeli military said it had killed two attackers, and another three soldiers had been lightly wounded in the attack. In a visit to Hebron after the attack, Mr Netanyahu said Israeli forces would enter the neighbourhood of the attackers and displace its residents. "We will evacuate the residents, we will go from house to house, we will also seize the weapons there, and all the terrorist infrastructure will be dealt with and destroyed," Netanyahu said, according to his office. "The defence minister and I are considering a very extensive IDF (army) operation in Judea and Samaria, such as has not been carried out since the Six Day War," Mr Netanyahu added, referring to the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. "The IDF is ready to execute it and we will set the timing, but it is on the way."

stories.title: Hanley: 'I thought we were gone to be honest'
stories.summary: Salthill-Knocknacarra manager Finian Hanley said he thought their day was over against Maigh Cuilinn in the first half when they failed to score against their opposition for the first 25 minutes of the Galway Senior Football Championship final. Reigning champions Maigh Cuilinn raced to a 0-04 unanswered lead, despite shooting into a strong breeze. However, the introduction of Tomo Culhane before the break dramatically changed the complexion of the game. Mark Mannion got them off the mark with a two pointer before Culhane added two of his own. "I was thinking would we score, that we mightn't win to be honest. We just couldn't get the shots off. Rob (Finnerty) was well curtailed in the first half. Eoghan Kelly did a fabulous job on him. Really frustrated him." Despite going into half-time with a 0-06 to 0-04 lead, it took Salthill-Knocknacarra until the final seconds of the game to secure a 2-12 to 1-14 victory. Peter Cooke scored a two-pointer for Maigh Cuilinn in the final minute of stoppage time but Hanley's squad went again and Culhane scored the match-winning goal.

Reigning [[curaidh|champions]] Maigh Cuilinn raced to a 0-04 unanswered lead, despite shooting into a strong breeze. However, the introduction of Tomo Culhane before the [[sos|break]] dramatically changed the complexion of the game. Mark Mannion got them off the mark with a two pointer before Culhane added two of his own. "I was thinking would we score, that we mightn't win to be honest. We just couldn't get the shots off. Rob (Finnerty) was well curtailed in the first half. Eoghan Kelly did a fabulous [[post|job]] on him. Really frustrated him." Despite going into half-time with a 0-06 to 0-04 lead, it took Salthill-Knocknacarra until the final seconds of the [[cluiche|game]] to secure a 2-12 to 1-14 [[bua|victory]]. Peter Cooke scored a two-pointer for Maigh Cuilinn in the final [[nóiméad|minute]] of stoppage time but Hanley's squad went again and Culhane scored the match-winning [[cúl|goal]].
